chapter: Chicago, Villa Venice and Louis Armstrong
title: How Budd got the Panama job from Henry Allen
summary: Henry Allen passed the Floyd Campbell job to Budd; the band was very good, shortly before joining Louis Armstrong in late 1932.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: band. So anyway, you know how I got that job, actually, with Floyd, he had first picked Henry Allen, the tenor sax@phone player, and Henry said, "Well look, man, you take the job. You know, because I'm going to do something else." So Floyd called me and that's how I really got the job.
I never will forget Henry Allen for that. He was a very fine young man, and a pretty good little sax@phone player.

But he finally went to Honolulu too, with that Bill Winston and all of the guys, and with the trumpet player who was -- had studied dentistry, or something, or no. He was a pharmacist at, oh, I'll think of his name, but you know who I'm talking about?

All of these cats went over to Honolulu. Anyway, we played around Chicago. This band became very, very good, and we worked in this little club, and the crowds were great, you know, so after this -- this must have been about 1932, the latter part of '32, because as I said before, Or I think I said to you, you know, after that then we joined Louis Armstrong.
